hook: Brewers Erase *Three* Leads, Seize NLCS Control
dek: Milwaukee overcame three Dodgers leads to win 7-4 and take a 2-0 NLCS lead.

slides.label: What happened
slides.text: The Brewers beat the Dodgers 7-4 in Game 2, erasing *three separate leads* to take control.

slides.label: Ace Chased
slides.text: Dodgers starter Yoshinobu Yamamoto was pulled after just *8 outs*, the shortest postseason start of his career.

slides.label: The Walk
slides.text: Jake Bauers fought through a *12-pitch at-bat* for a walk, then Christian Yelich singled him home for the lead.

slides.label: Contreras Delivers
slides.text: William Contreras crushed a *436-foot* game-tying homer off Kris Bubic, then added the go-ahead hit the next inning.

slides.label: Lockdown Bullpen
slides.text: Milwaukee's bullpen threw *five perfect innings*, the most ever by a team's pen in postseason history.

slides.label: The Numbers
slides.text: History favors Milwaukee: teams up *2-0* in a best-of-seven series win it *83%* of the time (79 of 95).

slides.label: What's Next
slides.text: The series shifts to Los Angeles for *Game 3* on Wednesday night. The Dodgers can't afford another loss.

slides.label: Why It Matters
slides.text: Milwaukee keeps proving grit beats hype, the same resilience underrepresented builders need when the odds say quit.

question: Will the Dodgers come back from 2-0? Yes or no?
first_comment: Fun fact: only two teams in postseason history have come back from a 2-0 deficit in the last three years, Blue Jays (2025) and D-backs (2023).

caption_instagram:
The Milwaukee Brewers put the Los Angeles Dodgers on notice. According to MLB.com, Milwaukee rallied from three separate deficits in Game 2 of the NLCS, beating the two-time defending champs 7-4 to take a 2-0 series lead.

Yoshinobu Yamamoto got chased after just 8 outs, the shortest postseason start of his career. Jake Bauers battled through a 12-pitch at-bat for a walk, Christian Yelich drove him in, and William Contreras delivered twice: a 436-foot game-tying homer and a go-ahead single. Milwaukee's bullpen finished with five perfect innings, the most ever by a team's pen in postseason history.

History says teams up 2-0 win the series 83% of the time, but comebacks do happen. Milwaukee isn't counting on luck, they're counting on resilience, the same resilience underrepresented builders need when the odds say quit.
